solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Troublesome child in quandary?

definitions.meaning: a 'little ...' is an informal British name for a mischievous child
to be in a fix or a predicament

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are everyday idioms: a mischievous little rascal, and a tricky fix one is stuck in.

clue.text: People put delicate fabric underneath uniform

indicators.note: in a down clue, underneath places the fabric below the letter for uniform

parts.note: to pop something somewhere is to put it there
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
lace is a delicate openwork fabric

explanation.surface: Someone sews delicate lace beneath a uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: The populace is the general public, the ordinary people of a place.

clue.text: Male swimmer — creature doing the crawl?

parts.note: a cock is a male bird
a roach is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A male swimmer doing front crawl in the pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the crawl' looks like the swimming stroke, but the creature crawls along the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: The insect scuttles along floors, so it is playfully a creature that crawls.

clue.text: Refuse family

definitions.meaning: refuse as a noun, rubbish dropped in the street
a family of young animals born together

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is scattered rubbish; the other is a brood of kittens or puppies born at one time.

clue.text: 12 record finished

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
over means ended, finished

explanation.surface: A cross-reference followed by a record that has stopped playing.
explanation.walkthrough: '12' points to the answer at 12-across, REALISE, which serves as the definition here.
explanation.definitionFit: To come to realise something is to find it out, a straight synonym for learning a fact.

clue.text: Union between races that is inspiring migrant, rare surprisingly

indicators.note: inspiring means breathing in, so the abbreviation takes the anagram inside it
surprisingly suggests an unexpected arrangement, so the letters of migrant and rare are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mixed marriage that inspires a migrant, which is surprisingly rare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' shuffles the two words into eleven letters, and 'inspiring' means the abbreviation breathes them in, sitting at either end.
explanation.definitionFit: Marriage across ethnic lines is exactly a matrimonial union of people of different races.

clue.text: For example, water bird circling land, briefly

indicators.note: circling means going round, so the bird's name surrounds the other piece

parts.note: a coot is a water bird

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter of land is dropped

explanation.surface: A water bird circles over land for a short while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' drops the last letter, and 'circling' wraps the bird round what remains. 'water bird' reads as one phrase, but water belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Water is a typical example of a liquid used to cool an engine or machine.

clue.text: Credentials minister backed up for Italian behind bars?

indicators.note: in a down clue, backed up means read from bottom to top, in reverse

parts.note: ID is identification, one's credentials
Rev, short for Reverend, is a title for a minister

explanation.surface: A minister's credentials are backed up for an Italian in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind bars' suggests prison, but the bars are musical: the composer of Aida stands behind bars of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe Verdi was an Italian opera composer, whose work is written in bars of music.

clue.text: Weapon good to stab back when raised

indicators.note: to stab means to pierce, so the letters for good go inside
in a down clue, raised means the word for back is read upwards, reversed

parts.note: the rear is the back
PI, short for pious, means good

explanation.surface: A weapon used to stab someone in the back when raised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when raised' gives RAER, read upwards in this down clue, and 'to stab' pierces it with the letters for good.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapier is a slender, sharp-pointed sword used for thrusting.

clue.text: Old Scot keeping Leader of Opposition in loop

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the Picts were an ancient people of what is now Scotland

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of Opposition

explanation.surface: An ancient Scotsman holds the Leader of the Opposition in a loop, a political picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader of Opposition' looks like a politician; it just gives the first letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: A picot is one of the small ornamental loops along the edge of lace or ribbon.

clue.text: Exhausted, do in left-back after match

indicators.note: after places the reversed piece behind the first one

parts.note: to fit is to match or suit

indicators.note: back means the preceding phrase is read in reverse order
in places the word do inside the word for left

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
taken as written

explanation.surface: A football picture: a left-back is worn out after the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left-back' looks like a football position. 'in' first gives PORDOT, and 'back' then reverses it to TODROP.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fit to drop is an idiom for being so tired one could collapse.

clue.text: Doing well, pass claimed by us — passing with those?

indicators.note: claimed by us means the pass is ours, so the possessive word follows the word for pass

parts.note: flying means doing very well, succeeding
a col is a mountain pass
ours means belonging to us

explanation.surface: Someone doing well in an exam passes, claiming the result for us.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the idiom: you pass an exam with flying colours.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass with flying colours is an idiom for succeeding brilliantly in a test.

clue.text: Unlawful act: criminal nearly accepting consequences, initially

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in, so one letter goes inside the anagram
criminal suggests something wrong or corrupted, so the letters of nearly are rearranged
initially picks the first letter of consequences

explanation.surface: A wrongdoer almost faces up to the consequences of an unlawful act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges NEARLY as LARENY, and 'accepting' puts C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Larceny is the legal term for theft, a crime of taking another's property.

clue.text: Make new serial, last of three

indicators.note: new means remade in a fresh form, so the letters of serial are rearranged
last of picks the final letter of three

explanation.surface: Instructions to produce a new TV serial, the final one of a trilogy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges SERIAL as REALIS, then the last letter of 'three' adds E.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise a sum, as in realising a profit, is to make or earn it.

clue.text: In leaving superpower, head for Djibouti, African country

indicators.note: leaving means the word in departs from the word for the superpower

parts.note: China is one of the world's superpowers
taken as written

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here of Djibouti

explanation.surface: A traveller leaves a superpower and heads for Djibouti, in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes IN out of CHINA, which leaves CHA.
explanation.definitionFit: Chad is a landlocked nation in north-central Africa.

clue.text: Soldiers in test rescuing lover

indicators.note: rescuing means holding something safe within, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: taken as written
to try is to test
a fan is a devoted lover of something

explanation.surface: Troops on a test mission rescue someone's beloved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rescuing' holds the lover between the two other pieces; 'in' is a piece of letters, not a containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The infantry are foot soldiers, the army's troops who fight on foot.

clue.text: Old song in recent memory?

definitions.meaning: as an adverb, on the day before today, very recently

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the Beatles' classic ballad; the other means the day just past, fresh in the mind.

clue.text: Fish not gutted, grouse cooked

indicators.note: cooked means prepared and changed, so the letters are rearranged
gutted means the insides removed, leaving the outer letters of not

explanation.surface: A recipe: fish left whole and grouse cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' leaves NT, and 'cooked' rearranges NT and GROUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The sturgeon is a large fish, famous as the source of caviar.

clue.text: Cold heart, obscene

parts.note: hard means cold and unfeeling, as in hard-hearted
the core of something is its heart

explanation.surface: Someone with a cold heart is described as obscene.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardcore pornography is the explicit kind, so the word describes material that is graphically indecent.

clue.text: Wheels turning, business working for American native

indicators.note: turning means the word for wheels is turned around and read backwards

parts.note: wheels is slang for a car
Co is short for company, a business
on means working, functioning

explanation.surface: A car's wheels turn as a business works for a Native American.
explanation.definitionFit: The ringed-tailed mammal is native to North America.

clue.text: Ship involved in exercise, I say!

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped up inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: PT is physical training, school exercise
SS is steamship, a standard ship prefix

explanation.surface: A ship takes part in an exercise and someone exclaims.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are ways of catching someone's attention quietly, an interjection meaning 'hey, listen'.

clue.text: Saint with halo in series

parts.note: a halo is a ring of light

explanation.surface: A saint wearing a halo appears in a series of paintings.
explanation.definitionFit: A string of events is a succession or sequence of them.

clue.text: Slightly sooner

definitions.meaning: somewhat, to a certain degree, as in 'a bit cold'
preferably, as in 'I would sooner stay'

explanation.definitionFit: The word means somewhat, and also means by preference in 'I'd prefer to'.

clue.text: One in better state, newsworthy

indicators.note: in places the numeral for one inside the other letters

parts.note: to top something is to better it
CAL is an abbreviation for California, a US state
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone in a better state of affairs makes the news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better state' reads as one phrase, but it is two pieces, with the numeral slipped between them by 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: A topical story concerns current affairs, so it is of interest in the news right now.

clue.text: Terrace: second in road I touch up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the pieces are read from bottom to top
second in picks the second letter of road

parts.note: taken as written
to tap is to touch lightly

explanation.surface: A terrace being touched up, the second one along the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses OITAP to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A patio is a paved outdoor area beside a house, much like a terrace.

clue.text: Lay a carpet on surfaces in every utility room

parts.note: taken as written
a mat is a small carpet

indicators.note: the surface of each word is its top, so the first letters are taken

explanation.surface: A DIY instruction to lay a carpet over the floor surfaces of every utility room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay' looks like a verb about fitting carpet; it is the adjective meaning non-professional.
explanation.definitionFit: Lay people are non-specialists, so lay is an adjective for someone without professional training.

clue.text: Present doctrine circulated around university

indicators.note: around means the anagram wraps the letter for university
circulated means moved around, so the letters of doctrine are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctrine is circulated around a university and presented to students.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circulated' rearranges DOCTRINE as INTRODCE, and 'around' puts U inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To present a person or topic is to bring it forward to others for the first time.

clue.text: Ultimately, bush on border?

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of bush

parts.note: an edge is a border

explanation.surface: A garden question: is this, in the end, a bush growing along the border?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: H plus EDGE, and a description of a row of bushes on a boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: A hedge is a line of shrubs planted along a boundary, so it is literally bushes on a border.

clue.text: Honour my word!

definitions.meaning: honour in the sense of virtue or moral worth
an exclamation of surprise, like 'gosh' or 'heavens'

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is moral virtue and integrity; the other is a mild oath of astonishment.

clue.text: Drawer that follows line, drawn back

indicators.note: follows places the word for that after the reversed piece
drawn back means the word for line is pulled back, read in reverse

parts.note: an arc is a curved line
yon is an old word for that, as in 'yon hill'

explanation.surface: An artist's tool that traces along a line and is then pulled back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawer' looks like a piece of furniture; it is something that draws.
explanation.definitionFit: A crayon is a stick of coloured wax used for drawing, so it is literally a thing that draws.
